text:
maria: heads-up: my local sample app is mis-ordering SSE chunks after a reconnect. UI shows partial text duplicated and sometimes out of order. repro is pretty reliable when i flip the network in devtools during a ~1k token response.
maria: raw log snippet i captured:
```
[2026-06-15T16:20:01.000Z] conn established id=dev-abc
[2026-06-15T16:20:02.100Z] sse id=1 data=...
[2026-06-15T16:20:02.400Z] client disconnected: ECONNRESET
[2026-06-15T16:20:02.700Z] reconnect rcvd resume_id=dev-abc rseq=1
[2026-06-15T16:20:02.900Z] sse id=3 data=...
[2026-06-15T16:20:03.050Z] sse id=2 data=...
[2026-06-15T16:20:03.200Z] sse id=3 data=... (duplicate)
```
maria: sample-app uses browser-sdk v0.9.7-dev and a naive stream reader:
```
const res = await fetch(url, { headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${token}` } });
const reader = res.body.getReader();
while(true) { const { done, value } = await reader.read(); if(done) break; handleChunk(value); }
```
maria: i tried persisting last-seen `id` and setting `Last-Event-ID` on reconnect; duplicates dropped but ordering still flips sometimes.
sam: do you get explicit `id:` lines from the server for every logical chunk? and is your proxy doing HTTP/2 or HTTP/1.1? could be multiplex reordering on the proxy side.
maria: server emits `id:` per chunk. local dev flow is http-proxy-middleware (node) -> staging runtime. i pulled a tcp dump: there were two overlapping HTTP/1.1 sockets (old conn hung, new reconnect opened); runtime wrote some tail chunks to both before noticing the old socket died.
kelsey: that maps to two likely causes: 1) race between auth refresh creating a parallel reconnect and old connection not fully drained; 2) proxy or runtime backpressure logic duplicating writes. infra should consider a guard: when a resume is detected, server should stop writing the same chunk to the old socket once the resume completes.
sam: on the client side we should: a) include Last-Event-ID on reconnects (explicit resume point), b) de-dupe on (id, length or hash) for safety, c) add jittered reconnect backoff so we don't stomp previous connections during auth refresh storms.
maria: noted. i'll push a sample-app PR that persists last id, sets Last-Event-ID, and keeps an LRU of seen ids to drop duplicates. i'll also bump to v0.9.8-dev.

maria: quick question: do we want the SDK streaming helper to offer built-in dedupe and resume handling? doing it in sample-app is fine but feels like a common pattern.
sam: yes please. SDK should expose an opt-in "robustResume" flag that stores last id, sends Last-Event-ID, dedupes by id, and adds small jitter to reconnects. keep it off by default until we validate.
kelsey: infra follow-up: i'll open an internal ticket to add server-side guardrails so we don't emit the same chunk to two sockets after a resume. include tcp capture + proxy config. i'll also check nginx/http-proxy-middleware behavior for connection draining.
maria: i uploaded tcp capture and proxy config to the new issue and linked PR: https://git.internal/redwood/sample-app/pull/172.
dev-bot: CI: sample-app-ci #672 passed (tests: 125) :rocket:
maria: thanks all. filing a short postmortem doc on the sample-app repo about recommended SDK/server resume semantics. tagging @kelsey for infra action. :thumbsup:
